questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere where i could understand the language, and improve my english. Therefore i chose Norway, because they meet my demands. I have also never been to Norway, and i really wanted to go.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy. I got emails saying what i needed to do, and I got a residence from the university. So it was a really safe start to the exchange.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a intro meeting, where we got information about the semester and what to expect. I was abroad with three friends, so we had each other for assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I was not easy, but it was durable. We used
hybel.no
and found an apartment where we could stay for 5 months. Often the contract was 1 year, so we were lucky.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really nice! But you definitely skip out on some social stuff, by living in your own space. We where four girls abroad together, and therefore we had each other. If i went by myself, I would have chosen to live on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We had to share a room, and that was why i chose to find my own place. I did not wanted to share a room with someone. I meet some friends which were sharing rooms, and they really liked it. So maybe it would have been an okay solution.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We just had to get the letter of arrival signed, and that is basically it. And then of course register for courses online, but that went pretty smooth.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a service desk, which were really sweet and helpfull. I think there were someone almost everyday 8-17 in the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Really successful, i got all the classes i really wanted. One course I heard there were a long waiting list for, but I got a spot, and it was such a nice course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is really easy, and everyone are so sweet. So do it! It is an amazing experience to study at University of Bergen

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses were pretty easy compared to my home university. I had a master course, which i did not found that difficult. With that being said, I learned a lot of new stuff. And some of the stuff was repetition from courses in Denmark, but it was nice to learn it one more time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was really similar. Lectures and seminars. But we had a lot more of oral presentations than in Denmark. I think i have had 2 presentations in Denmark in 2 years, and here i had 2 presentations in 1 semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I had the courses SDG213, ECON115 and GEO330

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend all the course. We were a lot of exchange students in these courses, and that was quite nice. I think i liked SDG213 the most, because we had lectures, seminars, to make a video and we had to make a thesis and present it. It was really nice to try out all the different types of learning, and i enjoyed that course a lot!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Trips! If you wanted to go somewhere it was more expensive than i had thought. And food. I hav used way more on food than i do in Denmark per month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
The electricity is quite expensive, and they only head up the buildings with EL. Other than that the alcohol is expensive and the food. 
Clothing and hiking stuff i cheaper here than in Denmark, which were quite nice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kind of sports, but you just had to go to a try out. You could join a choir as well. There were this event in the beginning, where all the sports activities and other campus stuff talked about their activities. It was really nice, because then you could find out what you wanted to join. I liked this a lot.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I played badminton, and liked it a lot. I have not played before, and the level was just chill and play. I think that was fun. Also go to the event in the start of the semester, because then you can find out if you want to join an organisation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike the 7 mountains around Bergen, that has been my favorite activity. And i also really like the bar Apollon and "Det akademiske kvarter" so cosy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Really easy. Norway is kind of similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open! Everyone is really sweet, you just have to give them a chance.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are really open and sweet. I liked that a lot. They made me fell welcome.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open. Studying is not everything. Hike and go on all the trips you can!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't meet that many norwegian students, but you meet a lot of exchange students. Which is a nice thing to know before you start.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning more about myself. It has been such a good experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Standing on my own two legs. I really learned a lot about myself, which were really really nice.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
